_meta.description: Website forms that submit into the object they name (decision 179, change website-forms-submit-into-tickets). A webForm names its own destination (a ticket, a lead, a contact or any other pipelinq object), with no fixed default (decision 181, Q4). Publishing one is checked against the destination schema by OpenRegister's FormDestinationValidator and refused on any finding (Q9). The ticket gains the reporter fields a website visitor types, so a website ticket can be answered. Three seed forms keep conduction-website's three existing forms working; an admin may point each at another destination.

webForm.title: Website form
webForm.summary: A public form and the object a submit creates
webForm.description: A form on a website or in Nextcloud Forms, and the pipelinq object each submit creates. The form names its destination and maps its fields onto that object's properties. Only mapped fields reach the object, so the mapping is the list of what a visitor may set. A published form is checked against the destination when it is saved: a form that could never produce a valid object is refused. There is no in-between store: a submit creates the destination in the request, or is refused.

title.title: Title
title.description: The form's name, as admins see it

key.title: Key
key.description: The name a website sends with each submit (the `source` field), for example website-support. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

status.title: Status
status.description: Only a published form takes submits. Publishing runs the destination check.

destination.title: Destination
destination.description: Where a submit goes: the register and schema slug of the object it creates, for example pipelinq and ticket.

writes.title: Writes
writes.description: For a form that creates several objects at once (a contact and a lead): each entry is { as, register, schema, mapping }. Used instead of destination and mapping; all are created or none.

mapping.title: Field mapping
mapping.description: fields: a list of { field, property, type, and the field's own limits such as maxLength }; fixed: property to value, set on every submit (for example channel: website).

fieldFallbacks.title: Field fallbacks
fieldFallbacks.description: field to a list of other fields: when the visitor leaves the field blank, the first filled one of the listed fields is used. For example a title taken from the organisation or name.

requireAnyOf.title: Required, one of
requireAnyOf.description: Fields of which the visitor must fill at least one, for example a message or an email address. Without it, any one mapped field will do.

audience.title: Audience
audience.description: Who may submit: anyone, or only signed-in users.

formsFormId.title: Nextcloud Forms form
formsFormId.description: When the answers come from Nextcloud Forms: the id of that form. Each field in the mapping is then a question id, and the binding is checked against the form's questions when it is saved.

reporterName.title: Reporter name
reporterName.description: The name the reporter typed, when nobody knows them yet (a website or form submit). Kept as typed; linking a contact stays a person's decision.

reporterEmail.title: Reporter email
reporterEmail.description: The email address the reporter typed. Usually the only way to answer a website submit.

reporterPhone.title: Reporter phone
reporterPhone.description: The phone number the reporter typed, if the form asked for one.

reporterOrganisation.title: Reporter organisation
reporterOrganisation.description: The organisation the reporter named, as typed.

source.title: Source
source.description: The form a submit came from (its key), for example website-support.

sourceUrl.title: Source page
sourceUrl.description: The page the form sat on when it was submitted.
